preamble: Prothesis of the voiceless velar fricative [x] before a word-initial vowel. The best-documented case is the sporadic x-prothesis of Persian, which predates Middle Persian (Middle Persian spelling still wavers between ʾyšm and xyšm 'anger') and also appears elsewhere in Southwestern Iranian. Because many of the affected roots began with a Proto-Indo-European laryngeal, some scholars treat individual items as laryngeal retentions or loans rather than true insertions, so the change is sporadic rather than a regular sound law.

examples.from: Avestan aēšəma, Old Persian *aišima 'wrath'; Middle Persian ʾyšm
examples.to: Middle Persian xēšm (xyšm), Persian خشم xašm [xæʃm] 'anger'
examples.note: Middle Persian attests both the vowel-initial and the x-initial spelling.

examples.to: Middle Persian xāyag, Persian خایه xāya [xɒːje]
examples.note: Listed by Cathcart (2022) as an example of the irregular pre-Middle-Persian x-prothesis.

sources: Cathcart, C. A. (2022). Dialectal layers in West Iranian: a Hierarchical Dirichlet Process approach to linguistic relationships. arXiv:2001.05297v4. https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.05297
